record.context_brief: Weak Lebesgue property for Hilbert spaces
record.original_question: For which cardinals κ does the Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ) have the weak Lebesgue property, meaning that every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → ℓ_2(κ) is weakly continuous almost everywhere?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. For which cardinals κ does the space ℓ_2(κ) have the WLP?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space. A function f:[0,1]→X is said to be Riemann integrable if there exists v∈X such that for every ε>0 there is δ>0 so that for every tagged partition 0=t_0<t_1<⋯<t_n=1 with mesh max(t_i−t_{i−1})<δ and any tags s_i∈[t_{i−1},t_i], one has ‖∑_{i=1}^{n}(t_i−t_{i−1})f(s_i) − v‖_X < ε. The function f is called weakly continuous at a point t∈[0,1] if for every continuous linear functional x*∈X*, the scalar function x*∘f is continuous at t. The space X is said to have the weak Lebesgue property (WLP) if every Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→X is weakly continuous at almost every t∈[0,1] with respect to Lebesgue measure on [0,1].

For a cardinal number κ, let ℓ_2(κ) denote the Hilbert space of all functions x:κ→ℝ such that {α∈κ : x(α)≠0} is at most countable and ∑_{α∈κ}|x(α)|^2 < ∞, equipped with the inner product ⟨x,y⟩=∑_{α∈κ}x(α)y(α).

Determine the class of cardinals κ for which ℓ_2(κ) has the weak Lebesgue property.
artifact.status_search_result: It is known that separable Hilbert space ℓ_2(ℵ_0) has the weak Lebesgue property, while any Banach space containing a closed subspace isomorphic to ℓ_2(c) fails the WLP, so ℓ_2(κ) lacks WLP for κ ≥ c. The status for cardinals ℵ_0 < κ < c does not appear to be fully resolved in the available literature, indicating the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Riemann integrability versus weak continuity
status_evidence.snippet: The weak Lebesgue property is stable under ℓ_1-sums; new examples of Banach spaces with and without this property are obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Active research identifies Banach spaces with/without WLP, but ℓ_2(κ) for general κ is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Weak Continuity of Riemann Integrable Functions in Lebesgue–Bochner Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Banach spaces containing ℓ_2(c) fail the weak Lebesgue property.
status_evidence.claim: ℓ_2(κ) fails WLP for κ ≥ c (continuum).
